finding.claim: DELETE /reports/:id authorization check is never enforced because authorize() is called without await, so any authenticated user can delete any report.

trace.note: DELETE route handler entered for any :id
authorize() called without await; its 403 rejection is never observed
authorize is async; grant check at lines 10-15 runs but result is discarded

finding.guards_checked: Grant check in authorize (server.js:10-15) is computed but discarded; no try/catch, no error handler, no route-level authz middleware; missing await is the decisive defect.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only candidate control is the grant check in authorize() at server.js:10-15, but it throws inside an async function, and the caller at server.js:20 does not await or catch it, so the rejection is unobserved and does not stop execution. No route-level authz middleware exists (server.js:4-7 only sets req.user). The DELETE handler's own resource load (server.js:19) has no ownership check either.
verdict.reason: authorize() at server.js:9-16 is async and throws on a missing grant, but the bare call at server.js:20 does not await it, so execution continues to db.reports.remove at server.js:21 and the report is deleted for any caller who reaches the route. The attacker only needs to reach the route; the candidate says "authenticated," which is accurate but narrower than the code allows, since req.user is not required to exist. The candidate omits a side effect: the unhandled rejection can crash the Node process on Node 15+ by default, though this does not change the bypass.

finding.claim: Unawaited and unhandled async rejections from authorize() crash the process under Express 4 on Node >=15, giving any unauthorized or malformed PUT/DELETE a service-wide DoS.
finding.source: Any HTTP client reaching port 3003 with PUT/DELETE; triggers: caller lacks grant, nonexistent id (null report), or missing req.user
finding.sink: Rejected promise from async route handler not caught by Express 4; unhandled rejection terminates process (server.js:20 DELETE, server.js:27 PUT)

trace.note: await authorize(...) rejects for unauthorized/null/undefined-user cases
resource.id or user.id access throws TypeError when report or user is null/undefined
403 error thrown when grants lack action
DELETE path: unawaited authorize rejection is unhandled by construction

finding.guards_checked: No Express 5 async error forwarding; no process.on('unhandledRejection') handler; no try/catch in either handler; no visible rate limit. Conditional on express version (package.json absent, unverified) and Node >=15.

verdict.guard_found: No guard in server.js catches the rejection. authorize() (server.js:9-16) throws on denial, but the DELETE call at server.js:20 is not awaited and nothing wraps it in try/catch. The PUT call at server.js:27 is awaited, but with no try/catch its rejection still escapes the handler. No process-level unhandledRejection handler exists. The only possible relevant control is the Express major version, which is not in this directory (Glob found no package.json).
verdict.reason: Every trace line checks out (server.js:10 throws on null resource, server.js:11-14 throws 403, server.js:20 is an unawaited authorize call, server.js:27 awaits it without a catch), but whether a rejection crashes the process depends on Express being v4 rather than v5, which auto-forwards async rejections to the error handler, and no package.json exists here to confirm the version. The attacker-reachability is also unclear: server.js:5 reads req.session.user with no session middleware in this file, so the claimed "anonymous" trigger would instead hit a sync TypeError that Express 4 turns into a 500; an authenticated low-privilege user is the realistic attacker.

finding.claim: PUT /reports/:id mass-assigns the entire request body to the record, letting a user with write grant alter any field including ownership or grant fields if the schema permits.

trace.note: JSON body parsed with no field allowlist
authorize(req.user, 'write', report) confirms write on this report only
full req.body passed to update; owner/grant/id keys written if schema allows

finding.guards_checked: Per-report write authorization at server.js:27 only; no field allowlist, no schema validation visible; schema not in corpus so severity is conditional (MEDIUM; raise to HIGH if owner or grant fields writable).

verdict.guard_found: Only per-report authorization at server.js:27 (`await authorize(req.user, "write", report)`), which checks write on this report and throws a 403 on failure. No field allowlist, schema validation, or body filtering exists between express.json() (server.js:3) and db.reports.update (server.js:28). The db module and schema are not in the corpus.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: req.body is parsed unfiltered at server.js:3 and passed whole to db.reports.update at server.js:28 after a write-grant check at server.js:27, so any user with write on a report can write arbitrary body keys. The claimed escalation to owner or grant fields at HIGH severity is unverified because the schema is not in the corpus, so the verified impact is mass assignment at MEDIUM severity.
